clue.text: Blue river follows a double bend

indicators.note: the river comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: the letter Z is shaped like a road sign's double bend
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A river's blue water runs on past an S-shaped curve in its course.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky shade, a synonym for that colour.

clue.text: Best choice of lines for booking?

definitions.text: Best choice of lines for booking?

parts.words: Best choice of lines for booking?
parts.note: reads like a travel agent's best rail routes, but means a book collecting selected poems

explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a published collection of selected poems or passages.

clue.text: Dim — not switched on

explanation.definitionFit: Something with no lamp burning is both dark and not turned on.

clue.text: There's some fear a cheat will prove a pain

indicators.note: some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone worries that a cheat will turn out to be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run inside 'fear a cheat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a specific ache in the ear, a kind of pain.

clue.text: Search for parking, " getting behindhand for rail connection

parts.note: to fish for something is to search for it
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
behindhand means late

explanation.surface: A driver hunting for a parking space ends up arriving late for a train connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray quote mark after 'parking,' is a printing blemish; 'getting' is a link word. A fishplate is the metal plate bolting two rail lengths together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishplate is the metal bar that joins two rail ends on a railway track.

clue.text: Last bit of almost excellent beer?

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: fine means excellent
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker savours the last drop of a nearly perfect pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a performance or work.

clue.text: Charming letter-writing

explanation.definitionFit: Casting enchantments and forming words correctly from letters are both covered by the term.

clue.text: A route into unspoilt fields?

indicators.note: the article and route letters go inside the word for unspoilt

parts.note: pure means unspoilt
ST, street, is a route

explanation.surface: A walking path leads into untouched countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; 'fields' looks plural but pasture is a mass noun for grazing land, so it stands in fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is grazing land, meadows where livestock feed.

clue.text: Chief has single, unadorned masculine name

parts.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
I is the Roman numeral one
bald means plain, unadorned

explanation.surface: The chief holds a single plain masculine title.
explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a traditional boy's given name of Scottish use.

clue.text: Sectarian, finally abandons East German town

indicators.note: the east letter is dropped from the end of the sect member

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ancient Jewish sect
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sectarian at last leaves East Germany for a western town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect; 'finally abandons' removes E (East) from the end of ESSENE. 'East German' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of Germany.

clue.text: Being indulgent with minor inaccuracy?

definitions.meaning: putting up with things patiently, forbearance
the small permitted margin of error in engineering measurement

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both forbearance toward others and the permitted variation in a machined dimension.

clue.text: Dismisses sound of jazz instrument

indicators.note: the sound of a word means it is heard, not spelt, so it is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: the sax, short for saxophone, is a jazz instrument

explanation.surface: Someone bans a saxophone's noise from the jazz club.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to fire them from a job, so sacks means dismisses.

clue.text: Measure island lake in reference to apparent anomaly

parts.note: an optic is a British pub device that dispenses a fixed measure of spirits

indicators.note: the island and lake letters go inside the word for reference

parts.note: an allusion is a passing reference

explanation.surface: A surveyor measures an island and its lake, noting a strange anomaly in the readings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container: the island and lake letters split the reference word after its second letter. An optic is the British pub gadget fixed to a spirit bottle that pours a single measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual trick that deceives the eye is something seen that seems real but is not.

clue.text: Begin to swap components to compensate

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase change places, front to back

parts.note: to set off is to begin a journey

explanation.surface: An instruction to start exchanging parts to make up for a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swap components' turns SET OFF into OFF + SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to balance or counteract it, making up for it.

clue.text: Rambling part of verse needing to be tightened up?

parts.note: a foot is a metrical unit of verse
something loose needs tightening

explanation.surface: A rambling section of poetry needs tightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means free to roam, wandering without ties.

clue.text: About to turn in complete work in concert

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the word for complete

parts.note: intact means whole, complete

indicators.note: the word for about is read backwards, giving ER

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A musician is about to hand in a finished piece of work at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' signals the reversal and 'in' the container. 'Concert' looks musical, but 'in concert' means together.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on one another, cooperating jointly.

clue.text: Normally mild, consumed with rage at first

indicators.note: the rage word comes first, before the consumed word

parts.note: temper means rage
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A normally gentle person is consumed by sudden fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate climate is one with moderate weather, not extreme.

clue.text: Pen lyric designed to be dignified

indicators.note: designed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A songwriter pens lyrics intended to sound stately.
explanation.definitionFit: Princely means stately and noble, befitting royalty.

clue.text: Gentlemen of yore, many in difficulties

indicators.note: being in difficulties suggests things gone awry, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: In olden days, many gentlemen fell on hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were the small landowning class of farmers, collectively a body of men below the gentry, here called gentlemen.

clue.text: A series of books are being written on the pole star…

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the last

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a series of books
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: Books are being written about the pole star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being written on' places A NT ARE above S in the down entry. Antares is a red star in Scorpius, not the Pole Star.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the brightest star in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Rarely rejected fashions worn by student

indicators.note: the student letter sits within the reversed fashions as though wearing them
rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: modes are fashions or styles
L is for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student rarely wears fashions others have rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MODES into SEDOM, and 'worn by' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means not often, an exact adverbial synonym.

clue.text: …while others take the lid off treasonable activity

indicators.note: removing the lid takes off the top letter of the word, first in a down entry

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state

explanation.surface: Meanwhile others uncover a treasonous plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 18: 'others' means other books of a series, issues of a work. 'take the lid off' drops the top letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a book is another printing, the other books published alongside the first series.

clue.text: Fail to hit a line, we hear, making poor stroke

indicators.note: we hear means the words are heard, so the sound-alike is entered

parts.note: miss means fail to hit, and a queue is a line

explanation.surface: A player misses the line and makes a bad shot.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS QUEUE said aloud gives the answer, a bad shot in snooker or billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty shot in billiards where the tip slips off the ball.

clue.text: One may have to carefully avoid such a solecism

definitions.text: One may have to carefully avoid such a solecism

parts.words: One may have to carefully avoid such a solecism
parts.note: the clue itself commits the grammatical fault it warns against, with an adverb wedged between to and its verb

explanation.definitionFit: Placing an adverb between to and its verb is the traditional grammatical blunder the clue names and commits.

clue.text: Mock food

definitions.meaning: slang for grub, something to eat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to deride and, informally, a meal or grub.

clue.text: I'm a success — in perfect form

parts.note: taken as written
to make a go of something is to make it a success

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being a triumph in peak condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The imago is the final adult stage of an insect, after metamorphosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists call the fully developed adult insect stage its perfect form.

clue.text: Circle with grim reputation

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
dour means grim, severe

explanation.surface: A gang circle carries a fearsome reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Odour as reputation comes from phrases like 'in bad odour', meaning out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean standing or repute, as in being in good odour with someone.

clue.text: Lead China in revolt? An outlandish course!

indicators.note: revolt suggests overturning, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A call to lead China into rebellion, dismissed as a bizarre course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' rearranges LEAD CHINA. 'Course' means a dish in a meal, and 'outlandish' says it is foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of rolled tortilla, a foreign meal course.

clue.text: Dislodges part of roof noisily, using any method

indicators.note: noisily means the words are heard, so their sound-alike is entered

parts.note: frees means dislodges and a tile is part of a roof

explanation.surface: A storm noisily knocks off a roof tile, using any means it can.
explanation.walkthrough: FREES TILE said aloud gives the answer. Freestyle swimming lets competitors use any stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In freestyle events competitors may choose whatever technique or stroke they like.

clue.text: Rope of onions initially has smell about it

indicators.note: the smell word goes round the onion letter

parts.note: to nose is to smell, sniff out

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of onions

explanation.surface: A string of onions gives off a strong smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives O from onions, and 'about' puts NOSE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a looped rope with a running knot.
